title: Automate multi-registry SDK release with signed attestations and ephemeral credentials
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Our current SDK release process for Python, TypeScript, and Go has ad-hoc steps across multiple CI jobs, static long-lived creds for registries (PyPI / npm / GOPROXY/GOMOD), and inconsistent artifact signing. This increases blast radius for credential leaks, makes reproducing builds difficult, and reduces trust in published packages.

Goal: Build a unified CI pipeline that can publish SDK artifacts to PyPI, npm, and Go module registries using ephemeral, OIDC-backed credentials; produce signed build attestations (Sigstore/cosign style) and SBOMs for each release; and expose per-language release recipes and examples so maintainers can run reproducible releases locally. The pipeline should include gating (automated checks + a human approval step) and automatic rotation/expiry of publishing credentials.

Success metrics: 
- No long-lived plaintext publishing keys stored in CI.
- All published releases include a signed attestation and SBOM (linked from package metadata) >= 90% of releases.
- Time-to-publish from tag to registry <= 10 minutes (CI time) for standard releases.
- Reproducible build guide validated by at least two engineers for each language.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline can publish to PyPI, npm, and Go module registry using OIDC / ephemeral credentials without any long-lived secrets in CI variables
Every published artifact includes a signed attestation (cosign or equivalent) and an SBOM stored alongside the release and referenced in package metadata
Automated checks: unit tests, integration smoke tests against a local runtime, license check, SBOM validity check, and a reproducible-build checksum verification step
Manual gate step present for public releases (requires 2 approvers), and can be bypassed for internal/nightly builds
Per-language release recipe docs (python, typescript, go) that reproduce CI steps locally and produce byte-for-byte reproducible artifacts
Example GitHub Actions workflows and pipeline templates checked into infra/ci with secrets policy and credential rotation docs
tasks: Design CI workflow with common build container and per-language job matrix
Integrate OIDC-based token exchange (GitHub Actions / cloud IAM) for ephemeral pub creds
Add cosign-based attestation signing step and define attestation schema
Generate SBOMs using SPDX/ CycloneDX for each package and sign them
Create reproducible build guide and local release script for maintainers
Add gating step with required approvals and audit logging
Add e2e test job that installs published packages from registries and runs smoke tests
Audit and remove existing long-lived CI registry credentials and rotate any exposed keys
